desc: Floor and dialogue: roles, the motion-handling dialogue cycle, obtaining/assigning the floor, preference in recognition, interruption rights, debate rights and per-member speech counters, decorum constraints on speech acts, and the voting/announcement exchange. The turn-taking wrapper around the engine: it decides who may speak and what speech act is admissible now; whether the CONTENT of a motion is in order is registry/engine/rules business. Per-motion interrupt/second attributes are registry ownership (Table t44-t45); this part consumes them via guard/in-order-when-other-has-floor.

roles.desc: presiding officer; grants recognition, states and puts questions, announces results, rules on order
full participant: attend, make motions, debate, vote
recording officer; reads papers on direction; records
contextual: member who made the pending motion
contextual: presents a board/committee report; motions on behalf of committee need no second
appointed vote-counter: distributes/collects/tallies ballots; first-line decider on ballot meaning (adjudication ballot-meaning, escalating to the assembly)

temporary occupant of the chair: elected at a mass meeting's organization [53:32], during the chair's relinquishment to debate [43:29], or under the 62:10 temporary-removal remedies; holds chair powers while occupying, not the office
no participation rights; presence at assembly's sufferance

roles_NOTE(judgment): maker/seconder/reporting-member are modeled as roles bound per-question, not global states; chair-pro-tem is an occupancy (who currently holds chair powers), distinct from the office — assembly.chair points at the occupant.

dialogue_cycle.desc: Six steps — three to bring before the assembly, three to consider [4:2, 4:25]. Emitted events named per step.

steps.rule: member with the floor states the motion [4:4]. Before stated, the motion is the maker's property: may modify or withdraw freely (withdrawn) [4:19, 33:12]; informal suggestions to modify/withdraw admissible without floor [4:20-23]

any member, no floor needed, without rising in small assemblies [4:9]. Not required when made by direction of a board/committee [4:11]. Absence of second becomes immaterial once debate begins or any member votes [4:13]

only the chair places the question before the assembly [4:3]; must state it promptly unless ruling it out of order or requiring clearer/written form (ruled-out-of-order alternative) [4:16-18]. After stated, ownership passes to the assembly [4:19]; withdrawal/modification now needs consent — see requests
if debatable (registry attribute). Maker has first-speech preference [4:27, 42:9(1)]

chair puts the question, exact wording definitive [4:34]; affirmative called first, negative always called (courtesy-motion relaxation noted; irrelevant-negative exception) [4:35]. Abstentions never called for [4:35]
report of voting, declaration, effect/execution statement, then next business [4:43-47]

unanimous_consent.rule: chair may take action or adopt absent objection — 'if there is no objection...'; a single member's objection forces the regular cycle; a timely objection overrides an already-made announcement [4:58-59]
unanimous_consent.NOTE(judgment): modeled as a compressed cycle emitting stated+put+adopted atomically, abortable by event/objected.

obtaining.rule: a member must be recognized before making a motion or debating; exceptions are the interruption-capable acts (interrupts below and Table t44-t45, registry-owned)
claim: rise after the floor is yielded, address the chair by title; identification in large assemblies; rising before the floor is yielded establishes no claim
chair must recognize a member entitled to the floor; assignment (event/recognized) by announcing name/identification, or a nod in small meetings
yield: resuming seat (event/floor-yielded); debate rights not transferable; unexpired time not reservable
recognition of the wrong claimant: remediable by motion/point-of-order; appealable except in mass meetings; assignment may be put to a vote when chair is in doubt (plurality wins the floor)
large-assembly adaptations (microphone queues etc.) are permitted variations, chair-directed pending rules

preference_in_recognition.desc: Applies only among members who rose before anyone was recognized [42:7]. Case selection by when_expr (first matching case governs); ladder entries within a case are strict priority order.

order.rule: maker of the immediately pending motion, if not yet spoken on it
order.variants: reporting-member for committee report; mover of take-from-table; mover (not caller-up) of reconsider

order.rule: member who has not spoken on this question today outranks one who has
alternate between opposing sides when known

rules.when: appeal or point-of-order submitted to assembly, debatable

order.rule: chair may speak first in preference to all, and again to close

order.exception: maker of reconsider moved for announced purpose of amending, upon reconsideration

order.rule: member rising to move retake of the vote by another method
member assigned to offer the called/prearranged main motion
member continuing a series of motions toward one object (e.g. after table/suspend-rules adopted for that purpose)
member whose announced alternative motion follows defeat of the prior motion
purpose-priority ladder, in order: (a) reconsider-enter-minutes, (b) reconsider, (c) call up reconsider, (d) give previous notice, (e) take-from-table, (f) motion with previous notice given

interrupts.desc: Only for listed purposes, urgency justifying [42:18-19]; interrupted speaker retains the floor and resumes after disposal (interrupted -> resumed, chair re-assigns) [42:20]. Handing a report to the secretary to read does not yield the floor [42:21]. Full per-motion interrupt/second data is registry ownership (t44-t45), consumed as guard/in-order-when-other-has-floor.

may_interrupt_speaker.act: demand separate vote on independent series / divisible amendments

speech_counters.modifiable_by: class/special-rules-of-order, or session/question orders via motion/limit-extend-debate

rules.rule: second speech barred while any member seeking floor has not spoken once on that question
each debatable motion in a series is a distinct question for counters
exhausted = 2 speeches that day on that question
rights renew entirely on a later day
asking a question, brief suggestion, or making a secondary motion without comment: not counted
questions answered by a speaker charge the speaker's time
no transfer or reservation of time
appeal: one speech per member, chair twice (close)
committee-of-whole/quasi/informal speeches don't count against same-day assembly rights
reconsider debate rights separate from original consideration; same-day reconsideration re-imports exhaustion for the reconsidered question

speech_counters.lifecycle_interaction: postponement or table+resume to a DIFFERENT day renews rights; same-day resume preserves exhaustion [14:19, 34:6] (state carried by lifecycle; counters owned here)

requests.withdraw_modify: after stated: request by maker; unanimous-consent attempt first, else vote on granting [33:11-19]. Withdrawal admissible until voting begins; adhering motions fall with it [33:16]. Withdrawn motion = never made (renewal unrestricted) [33:18, 38:2]
requests.inquiries: parliamentary inquiry / request for information: no vote; chair responds or channels to a member; third-person exchange through the chair [33:3-10]
requests.other: read papers / other privileges: consent or majority [33:20-22]

decorum.desc: Admissibility filters on debate content. Content compliance is judgment-shaped: breaches enter via ["adjudged", "decorum-breach", speech-act] (adjudication.json); these rules are the declared standards the adjudication applies.

rules.rule: germaneness to the immediately pending question
no personalities; no questioning motives; measure-not-member
all remarks through the chair; no direct member-to-member exchange
avoid names; officers by title; chair never addressed as 'you', speaks of self in third person
no adverse comment on a prior act not pending unless concluding with a motion to reconsider/rescind/amend it or notice thereof
maker may not speak against own motion (may vote against)
chair does not debate while presiding; must relinquish chair to do so, not returning until the main question is disposed of; exception: appeals and submitted points of order
enforcement path on breach: call to order -> permission-to-continue vote -> naming, escalating to rules/disciplinary territory
interruption of voting barred from first vote cast until polls presumed complete (guard/voting-in-progress); no explanation of votes during voting
vote changeable until result announced; afterward only by unanimous consent, requested immediately

challenge window: point-of-order on the conduct of a vote, division demand, retake motion, recapitulation, vote change — all only until debate or business intervenes (event/challenge-window-closed), except continuing breaches

division of the assembly: single member's demand (event/division-demanded), from the moment the negative is cast until immediately after announcement, compels a rising retake (event/vote-retaken); dilatory-use filter
inconclusive-vote ladder (chair-driven): voice -> 'seem to have it' pause -> rising -> counted rising
